en: The Sūtra on the Ambrosial Drum of the True Dharma of the Stūpa-Pavilion,
spoken by the Buddha. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Mingjiao Dashi,
the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Tianxi Cai, at the Mi-lin Monastery in the kingdom of Jālandhara, Central India.
Translated by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard:
At one time, the World-Honored One was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, having aroused a heart of sincere truth, went to where the World-Honored One was.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he prostrated his head at the feet of the World-Honored One.
Having completed his acts of reverence, he stood to one side.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"How does one plant pure roots of virtue?
How does one construct a maṇḍala?
How does one take refuge and undertake the training precepts?"
How is it that by joining the ten fingers and palms together to pay respectful homage to the Tathāgata, one accomplishes wholesome karma?
World-Honored One!
How is it that the roots of goodness within saṃsāra do not perish?
"How does one attain nirvana through the exhaustion of karma?
What are the merits of creating an image of the Tathāgata?
The World-Honored One replied:
“Ānanda! You should cultivate and maintain five virtues with purity.

Furthermore, it is said that by using such speech, one awakens the mind of oneself and the minds of others, causing the noble ones to rejoice; one’s wholesome karma becomes magnificent, all that is sought is attained, and at the dissolution of the body after death, one is reborn in the heaven of the Sugata.”

Ānanda! If there are those who, having resolved their minds for the sake of the Buddha, extend offerings by constructing a four-sided maṇḍala, I declare that such persons shall, in a future age, become lords of wealth and nobility in Uttarakuru, and after the dissolution of the body, be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.

Ānanda! If there are those who, having resolved their minds for the sake of the Buddha, extend an offering by constructing a maṇḍala in the shape of a half-moon, I declare that such persons, in a future life, shall become lords of wealth and nobility in Pūrvavideha, and after the dissolution of the body, they shall be reborn in the Yāma Heaven.

Ānanda! If there are those who, having resolved their minds for the sake of the Buddha, extend offerings by constructing a circular maṇḍala, I declare that such persons, in a future age, shall become lords of wealth and nobility in the western continent of Aparagoyānī, and after the dissolution of their bodies, they shall be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.

Ānanda! If there are those who, having resolved their minds for the sake of the Buddha, extend offerings by constructing a maṇḍala in the shape of a chariot, I declare that such persons shall, in a future age, become lords of wealth and nobility in Jambudvīpa in the south, and after the dissolution of the body, be reborn in the Heaven of Delighting in Transformations (Nirmāṇarati).

Ānanda! If there are those who take refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and maintain the pure precepts, I declare that their roots of goodness and merit are immeasurable and boundless; all Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, even until the limit of Nirvāṇa, would be unable to calculate them.
At that time, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:

“Know according to your own understanding: those red lotuses are soft and stainless, and the leaves of the aśoka tree are of a subtle copper hue; my tongue is like them, extending so as to cover the face up to the hairline, just as you have seen.”
Ānanda! Who could possess such [a tongue] through false speech, frivolous speech, harsh speech, or divisive speech?
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, speaks only what is true; his tongue is indeed like this.

Ānanda! If there are those who take refuge, join their palms in prostration, and pay homage to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—those sentient beings who thus take this refuge shall be saved by me.
Why is this? Ānanda!
Because the Tathāgata’s dharma-realm is definitive; if one possesses sincerity and resolve, and performs prostrations with palms joined or offers gifts, [the merit will be immeasurable].

"Ānanda! Furthermore, suppose there is someone who, while washing their hands or rinsing out various vessels, for that brief moment generates the aspiration to benefit living beings, vowing that all sentient beings may attain peace and happiness. Ānanda!"
I say that such a person opens the gate of merit and closes the gates to the evil realms, thereby escaping three kalpas.
What are these three kalpas?
They are the kalpa of weapons, the kalpa of pestilence, and the kalpa of famine.
Ānanda! Furthermore, if there is someone who observes this precept of abstaining from taking life for even a single day, that person will not be born during the kalpa of weapons;
if one gives a single harītakī fruit as an offering to the Saṃgha, that person will not be born during the kalpa of pestilence.
If one offers a single bowl of food and drink to the Saṃgha, that person shall attain rebirth in an age free from famine.
"Ānanda! There are three roots of goodness that are inexhaustible and boundless; even while remaining within saṃsāra, they do not perish, and one shall thereby proceed toward Nirvāṇa."
Ānanda! What are these three? They are:
planting roots of goodness in the Tathāgata that are inexhaustible and boundless; not being extinguished even while dwelling within saṃsāra; and ultimately proceeding toward nirvāṇa.

The roots of goodness planted toward the Dharma and the Sangha are likewise inexhaustible and boundless; even while remaining within saṃsāra, they shall never perish, and in the future, one will surely attain nirvāṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One, by means of the Tathāgata’s merit, said to Ānanda:
"Do you see that Jambudvīpa in the south?
Ānanda replied to the World-Honored One:
“Yes, indeed, I have seen it! “Ānanda!

Suppose there were a son or daughter of noble family who, having fashioned the continent of Jambudvīpa out of the seven precious gems in the shape of a chariot, measuring seven thousand yojanas in length and breadth, used it as a gift to make offerings to the Saṅgha of the four quarters, as well as to stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and even pratyekabuddhas;”
If, after a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has entered parinirvāṇa, one were to fashion a stūpa from a lump of clay as large as an āmalaka fruit—
with a parasol finial (caitya-yaṣṭi) as small as a needle, a canopy like a jujube leaf,
and a Buddha image within as small as a grain of barley;
"Enshrining the śarīra like white mustard seeds—I declare that this merit is vast and superior to that. Ānanda!
Let us set aside Jambudvīpa for a moment."

Ānanda! Suppose there were a son or daughter of noble family who, having fashioned the eastern continent of Pūrvavideha out of the seven precious substances—shaped like a half-moon on all four sides and measuring exactly eight thousand yojanas in length and breadth—were to offer it as a gift to the Saṃgha of the four directions, as well as to those who have attained the fruits of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, Arhat, up to Pratyekabuddhas;

and suppose that after the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha has entered parinirvāṇa, they were to fashion a stūpa from a lump of clay the size of an āmalaka fruit, with a parasol (chattrāvalī) placed upon it as small as a needle.
Covering it with a parasol like a jujube leaf,
placing a Buddha image within like a grain of wheat,
and enshrining the śarīra relics below like white mustard seeds.
"I say that this merit is vast and superior to that.
Ānanda! Let alone Jambudvīpa in the south and Pūrvavideha in the east."

Ānanda! If there are faithful sons or daughters of noble family who fashion the continent of Aparagoyānī out of the seven precious jewels, making it as full as the moon and nine thousand yojanas in length and breadth, and offer this as a gift to the Saṃgha of the four quarters—including stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners, arhats, and even pratyekabuddhas;

and if, after the parinirvāṇa of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, they were to fashion a stūpa from a lump of clay the size of an āmalaka fruit, with a harmikā like a needle and a parasol like a leaf; [the latter would be far more meritorious].
If one places an image of the Buddha within [the stupa] like a grain of barley,
and enshrines śarīra relics below it like white mustard seeds— I declare that this merit surpasses the former.
“Ānanda! Let us set aside for now Jambudvīpa in the south, Pūrvavideha in the east, and Aparagoyānī in the west. Ānanda!”

If there were sons or daughters of noble family who, using the seven precious jewels, fashioned the continent of Uttarakuru—each of its four sides measuring ten thousand yojanas—and with this offered worship to the Saṃgha of the four directions, as well as to those in the stages of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, Arhat, up to Pratyekabuddha;

and if, after the Parinirvāṇa of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, they were to fashion a stūpa from a lump of clay the size of an āmalaka fruit—with its harmikā like a needle and its parasol like a leaf;
and place within it an image of the Buddha the size of a grain of barley; [the merit of the latter would be far greater].
If one were to enshrine the *śarīra* relics like white mustard seeds—I say that this merit would be vast and superior to that. "Ānanda!
Let alone those four great continents."

If there were sons or daughters of noble family who, having fashioned the Sudharmā Hall of Śakra, Lord of Devas, out of the seven precious gems, offered it as a gift to the Saṃgha of the four directions, as well as to those who have attained the stage of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, Arhat, and even up to Pratyekabuddhas;

and if, after the Parinirvāṇa of a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, they were to fashion a stūpa from a lump of clay the size of an āmalaka fruit—adorned with various features such as the harmikā, the parasol, and the spire, and containing a Buddha image and enshrined relics, no different from the former case—I declare that this merit would be vast and superior to the other.
“Ānanda! Let alone those four continents and the Sudharmā Hall;
Ānanda! [let alone that].”

If there are sons or daughters of noble family who possess faith, and even were they to take those seven precious jewels and fashion them into a trichiliocosm to offer as alms to the Saṃgha of the four directions, as well as to those from the four fruits of the path up to the pratyekabuddhas;

or if, after the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha has entered parinirvāṇa, one were to use a lump of clay to construct a stūpa the size of an āmalaka fruit—adorned with various features such as the *cakra* and parasols, enshrining a Buddha image and the relics of his cremation, exactly as described before without difference—I declare that this merit is vast and superior to the former.
For what reason? Ānanda!

The Tathāgata’s generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and all-knowledge are immeasurable and boundless; even his ten powers, four types of knowledge, three unique qualities, and four foundations of mindfulness, up to and including his great compassion, are likewise immeasurable and boundless. It is because the Tathāgata possesses such meritorious qualities!
“Ānanda! When the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha taught this Dharma, the trichiliocosm shook throughout its entirety.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What should this True Dharma be named?
How should it be upheld?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"This sutra is named 'The Drum of the Ambrosia of the True Dharma,' and it is also named 'The Unprecedented True Dharma.
Thus should you receive and uphold it!"
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda, with a mind of rare wonder, received the Buddha’s holy instruction, accepted and upheld it with faith, prostrated himself, and withdrew.
*The Sūtra of the Ambrosial Drum of the True Dharma of the Pavilion*, spoken by the Buddha.
